headline: High: Mentat can write shared files and use broad network egress, creating default risks of data leakage and cascading errors when paired with dbt-core’s warehouse-facing workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core has no documented shared channel or parser for Mentat outputs, and Mentat’s bridge is mainly files/stdin-stdout. The only plausible injection path is manual copy-paste or shared files, so the blast radius is limited and not default. Both agents lack a documented direct instruction channel.
conditions: IF an operator copies dbt-core-generated text into Mentat prompts or files, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace, file-based instruction smuggling becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep dbt artifacts and Mentat prompts in separate directories.
Review any copied SQL/model text before pasting into Mentat.
Use read-only exports for dbt outputs when possible.
Add a short prompt prefix telling Mentat to ignore instructions in files.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for generated artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat reads and writes local files and sends prompts to a configured model provider, while dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted egress. If warehouse-derived files are placed in Mentat’s workspace, sensitive data can flow into model-provider requests. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default workflows, though not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF warehouse-derived dbt artifacts are opened by Mentat, those contents can be transmitted to the model provider.
IF the allowlist includes the warehouse endpoint used by dbt-core, data can traverse both agents’ network paths.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive warehouse extracts in Mentat’s working directory.
Use masked or sampled dbt outputs for coding assistance.
Restrict Mentat to non-sensitive repos only.
Verify the model provider logging/retention settings before use.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before model-provider calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model shares state via filesystem. dbt-core is not a writer to the same local workspace, but it does operate on warehouse data and can coexist in the same project tree. The overlap is enough for file and git contention if both touch the same repo, though not a high-risk unrestricted conflict.
conditions: IF dbt-core-generated files and Mentat edits target the same git checkout, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF multiple Mentat instances run on the same filesystem, state collisions can occur.
mitigations: Serialize edits to one checkout at a time.
Use separate branches for dbt and Mentat work.
Commit or stash before launching another Mentat session.
Keep generated dbt artifacts out of tracked paths.
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared workspaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat is a diff-based coding assistant that can act on file contents, while dbt-core produces analytics artifacts that Mentat may treat as authoritative inputs. If dbt outputs are fed into Mentat without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect code changes or commits. The pathway exists in default workflows, but the blast radius is usually bounded to work products.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs are used as source material for Mentat edits without review, incorrect assumptions can propagate.
IF Mentat is allowed to commit or propose diffs based on unverified dbt artifacts, downstream errors can persist.
mitigations: Require human review of dbt outputs before editing code.
Cross-check generated SQL against source models.
Use small, isolated diffs for Mentat changes.
Run tests after each accepted diff.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between analytics outputs and code edits.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch. dbt-core touches warehouse data, while Mentat handles source code and model-provider keys, so compliance risk is mainly operational logging/retention rather than a documented jurisdiction breach. No direct cross-border or regulated-data violation is evidenced here.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is copied into Mentat prompts, retention and logging policies must be rechecked.
IF the configured model provider stores prompts outside the required jurisdiction, compliance obligations may change.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to Mentat.
Confirm provider retention settings before use.
Use synthetic or redacted examples for coding help.
Document which datasets may enter prompts.
requires-engineering: enforce jurisdiction-aware routing and retention controls.
